records.finding: GAO reports that DOE implemented five of thirty prior priority recommendations, added one priority recommendation, removed priority status from two, and now has twenty-four priority recommendations.
records.decision: Publish the exact portfolio movement while keeping implemented, newly added, de-prioritized, and currently prioritized states distinct.
records.remaining_gap: Action-level identities and closure evidence for the current twenty-four, including DOE insider-threat recommendations 1 and 7 and the separate AI-inventory action.
records.reopening_rule: Reopen when GAO publishes the next DOE priority letter or changes a named current recommendation status.

records.entity_name: Department of Health and Human Services
records.finding: GAO reports that HHS implemented four of thirty-five prior priority recommendations, added seven, and now has thirty-eight priority recommendations focused on program integrity and public-health oversight.
records.decision: Publish the exact portfolio movement without treating it as clinical, provider, or preparedness performance.
records.remaining_gap: Action-level closure evidence for the thirty-eight priorities, the open AI-inventory action, and a post-July 29 public update for the four held hospital-control recommendations.
records.reopening_rule: Reopen when GAO publishes the next HHS priority letter, changes a named priority status, or HHS OIG posts the held hospital-control update.

records.finding: GAO reports that DOT implemented three of twenty-one prior priority recommendations, added six, removed priority status from two, and now has twenty-two priority recommendations.
records.decision: Publish the exact portfolio movement while preserving workforce, grants, drones, automated-vehicle, and AI-inventory scopes.
records.remaining_gap: Action-level closure evidence for the current twenty-two, the open AI-inventory action, and the FY 2026 information-security review result.
records.reopening_rule: Reopen when GAO publishes the next DOT priority letter, changes a named recommendation status, or DOT OIG publishes the FY 2026 review result.

records.finding: GAO reports that VA implemented two of twenty-nine prior priority recommendations, added three, and now has thirty priority recommendations across health-care access, IT modernization, and acquisition management.
records.decision: Publish the exact portfolio movement without substituting it for iFAMS, Southern Oregon, enterprise FISMA, or veteran-outcome evidence.
records.remaining_gap: Action-level closure evidence for the thirty priorities, the open iFAMS recommendations, and Southern Oregon recommendations 1, 2, 5, 6, and 7.
records.reopening_rule: Reopen when GAO publishes the next VA priority letter or VA OIG changes the named iFAMS or Southern Oregon recommendation states.

records.finding: GAO reports that GSA implemented two of eight prior priority recommendations, removed priority status from one, added six, and now has eleven priority recommendations.
records.decision: Publish the exact portfolio movement as federal shared-services and award-oversight context.
records.remaining_gap: Action-level identities and closure evidence for the eleven current priorities and operating outcomes for real property, shared services, awards, and procurement channels.
records.reopening_rule: Reopen when GAO publishes the next GSA priority letter or a named current recommendation changes status.

records.entity_name: Office of Science and Technology Policy
records.finding: GAO reports that OSTP implemented three of six prior priority recommendations, added one, and now has four priority recommendations focused on national science-and-technology goals and research security.
records.decision: Publish the exact portfolio movement while keeping national-goal tracking and research-security information sharing separate.
records.remaining_gap: Action-level closure evidence for the four current priorities and measured outcomes from national-goal tracking or research-security coordination.
records.reopening_rule: Reopen when GAO publishes the next OSTP priority letter or a named current recommendation changes status.

records.finding: GAO reports that NTIA implemented one of eleven prior priority recommendations and now has ten priorities across spectrum, IT and cybersecurity, and broadband programs.
records.decision: Publish the exact portfolio movement without converting one implementation into an infrastructure-security or broadband-performance conclusion.
records.remaining_gap: Action-level closure evidence for the ten priorities and operating measures for spectrum coordination, infrastructure security, and broadband-program sustainability.
records.reopening_rule: Reopen when GAO publishes the next NTIA priority letter or a named current recommendation changes status.

records.status_period: Open recommendations as of October 2025; report published May 2026
records.finding: GAO estimates that implementing open recommendations could produce $132 billion to $251 billion in measurable future financial benefits; the range is model-based, excludes many nonquantifiable benefits, and is not realized savings.
records.decision: Publish the modeled range as bounded government-wide context with the method and realization limits attached.
records.remaining_gap: Recommendation-level implementation, attribution, timing, realized savings, nonfinancial outcomes, and agency-specific allocation of any benefit.
records.reopening_rule: Reopen when GAO updates the model, publishes realized benefit attribution, or materially revises the open-recommendation inventory.
